title: Graceful shutdown with signal handling and request draining
description: Adds support for SIGTERM/SIGINT handling so the server can stop accepting new connections, finish in‑flight requests, and close resources cleanly. This reduces abrupt termination errors and improves reliability in containerized deployments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while requests are pending and verify that new connections are rejected but existing ones complete before process exit
Trigger SIGINT during idle state and ensure the server closes all listeners and releases resources without errors
acceptance: When the process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the framework stops accepting new requests, waits up to a configurable timeout for active requests to finish, then closes all listeners and resolves a shutdown promise. All tests pass and no unhandled promise rejections occur.
reason: Production environments (Docker, Kubernetes, serverless) rely on graceful termination to avoid data loss and 5xx spikes during redeploys. Implementing this feature makes yantraverse ready for enterprise‑grade deployments without external tooling.
